name: spawn_agent
description: Creates a temporary sub-agent to carry out a specific task. The sub-agent works independently and returns a report. You can specify a predefined character, or a custom role and trait.

task.description: The specific task to assign the sub-agent, as a short inline text. Limit: 2000 characters. If that's not enough, do NOT shorten it (requirements get silently lost): split it into multiple spawn_agent calls (one per self-contained task), or use 'briefingFile' for a long briefing. If 'briefingFile' is present, 'task' is optional and acts as a short introduction ahead of the file's content.

briefingFile.description: Path to a file (written beforehand with write_file) containing the full briefing for the sub-agent. Use it for long or detailed tasks instead of pasting everything into 'task': a path is a short string, easy to generate without formatting errors; a long briefing pasted inline into 'task' risks breaking the JSON generation of the call itself. Limit: 12000 characters in the file.

charName.description: Name of the predefined character to use, as it appears in the installed catalog; alternatively, the required role/craft (e.g. 'security_auditor'). Optional: if omitted, uses the specified role and trait.

roleName.description: Role for the sub-agent (e.g. 'developer', 'sysadmin'). Used only if charName is not specified.

traitName.description: Trait for the sub-agent (e.g. 'creative', 'grumpy'). Used only if charName is not specified.

reasoningEffort.description: Reasoning effort imposed on the sub-agent for THIS task, overriding the character/role. Optional: if omitted, the sub-agent inherits the normal cascade (character -> role -> default). Lower it to 'none' or 'low' for mechanical tasks (applying an already-known change, reformatting a file, extracting fields from text): having a sub-agent reason at length over a mechanical task is just wasted time. Leave it at 'medium'/'xhigh' only if the task genuinely requires analysis or planning.
